search_log: Searched: "Anne Rice Merrick novel excerpt David Talbot narrator first person" and "Merrick Anne Rice first person narrator point of view"; found the authorized Knopf opening excerpt and explicit narrator descriptions.

Searched publisher and author domains with: site:penguinrandomhouse.com Merrick Anne Rice excerpt and site:annerice.com Merrick narrator; the Penguin Random House Higher Education page timed out when opened, while Anne Rice's archived phone transcript opened successfully.
Searched: "Merrick Anne Rice review narrator David Talbot" and "Merrick Anne Rice told by David Talbot review"; opened Publishers Weekly and Bookreporter reviews confirming the whole-book narrator.

Ran targeted exact-phrase searches for potentially clipped or misleading quotes, including "There are so many books I mean to read," "I hear the birds singing," "I've been too young for too long," and "Elements we might call Asian or Chinese," to distinguish dialogue and embedded writing from David's narration.

Google Books supplied bibliographic and synopsis material but no useful sustained interior preview. A searchable third-party scan was consulted only to resolve local quotation boundaries and was not treated as classification evidence.
person_note: The controlling narrator is David Talbot, who participates throughout and recounts both the present action and extended memories in first person. Numerous interior Goodreads passages independently expose David's I/we narration, while the authorized opening names him as the tale's author and multiple whole-book sources identify him as narrator. Apparent contrary first-person voices are local material: Lestat, Louis, and Merrick speak in dialogue, while Aaron's notes and Merrick's report are embedded documents. The novel alternates timelines and recollection with present action, but the evidence does not show sustained base sections in another grammatical person. Remaining uncertainty is limited to a few clipped quote boundaries and does not affect the book-level label.
